package_info.package_versions: Malicious versions published May 21-22, 2022 (exact versions not specified)
package_info.why_malicious: The package was hijacked via a PyPI account takeover and injected with code that, upon import, exfiltrates all environment variables—including sensitive credentials such as AWS keys—to an attacker-controlled external server.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code imports the os and requests modules, collects all environment variables using os.environ, and sends them via HTTP POST to anti-theft-web.herokuapp.com, resulting in exfiltration of sensitive environment data to an external attacker-controlled server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code automatically collects all environment variables and transmits them to an untrusted external domain without user knowledge or consent, which is a clear indicator of credential theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate package should not access or transmit environment variables during import, nor should it make unsolicited network requests to non-official domains in initialization code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some diagnostic or debugging tools may access environment variables for local troubleshooting, but they do not transmit this data externally without explicit user approval.
key_indicators: Access to all environment variables via os.environ
Unsolicited HTTP POST request to anti-theft-web.herokuapp.com
Network activity triggered during package import
No user interaction or notification before exfiltration

attack_chain.action: Attacker compromises the PyPI account for the ctx package and publishes a new version containing malicious code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Maliciously modified ctx package is distributed to users via PyPI.

attack_chain.action: User installs or imports the ctx package, which triggers the execution of the malicious code at import-time.
attack_chain.leads_to: The malicious code collects all environment variables from the user's system.

attack_chain.action: The malicious code sends the collected environment variables, including sensitive credentials, to the attacker's server at anti-theft-web.herokuapp.com.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive environment data and credentials, enabling further exploitation.

behavioral_signatures: Import-time or install-time network requests to untrusted or non-official domains
Access to all environment variables (os.environ) in package initialization code
Exfiltration of environment data via HTTP POST during package import
file_indicators: ctx/__init__.py containing both os.environ and requests.post
Hardcoded references to anti-theft-web.herokuapp.com in source code
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP POST requests to anti-theft-web.herokuapp.com during package import or installation
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Use static analysis to identify packages that access os.environ or similar environment variable collections in initialization files and combine this with detection of network requests (e.g., requests.post) to non-official domains. Monitor for outbound HTTP POST requests to anti-theft-web.herokuapp.com or similar suspicious domains during package import or installation. Flag any package that transmits environment data externally without user interaction or consent.
